purpose: Non-admission review of external original datasets and access leads found while auditing 20 peer catastrophe-risk, disaster-data, satellite-damage and insurance model repositories. Software references are not dataset admissions; accepted existing GEM GEID, GFDRR Risk Data Library and Oasis/USGS source identities are not duplicated.

entries.name: IFRC Montandon Global Crisis Data Bank event, hazard and impact API
entries.spatial_scope: global, depending on upstream source and reporting completeness
entries.temporal_scope: historical and current event, hazard and impact records; provider vintages vary
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Linked disaster event/hazard/impact records, country and spatial joins, multiple original source IDs
entries.note: IFRCGo/GCDB performs multi-provider ETL; IFRCGo/monty-stac-extension and IFRCGo/pystac-monty implement STAC event/hazard/impact relationships. Montandon requires an IFRC GO token due to upstream restrictions. Check ETL provenance, original ID, impact type, known-at time and allowed redistribution separately. Do not merge related earthquakes or treat a humanitarian impact estimate as insured loss. Discovery: https://github.com/IFRCGo/GCDB ; https://github.com/IFRCGo/monty-stac-extension ; https://github.com/IFRCGo/pystac-monty.

entries.name: CLIMADA Data API v2 hazard and exposure dataset catalogue
entries.spatial_scope: global for selected datasets, spatial/time coverage differs by product
entries.temporal_scope: historical, present and future climate scenario sets; dataset and version specific
entries.resolution_or_granularity: API v2 dataset IDs and metadata, downloadable input files and event-set references
entries.note: Official data API documents v2 dataset and data_type endpoints. Provider publicly describes CC BY 4.0 data and GPL-3.0 software; verify each dataset's upstream provenance, units, spatial support, source licences, climate scenario and revision before admission. CLIMADA hazard sets are not automatically independent of copied IBTrACS or other underlying providers; 4 km products cannot be assumed building-resolution. Code: https://github.com/CLIMADA-project/climada_python ; https://github.com/CLIMADA-project/climada_petals.

entries.name: GFDRR ThinkHazard multi-peril administrative hazard scores
entries.spatial_scope: global with national and subnational availability depending on selected layer
entries.temporal_scope: periodic screening scores; hazard and underlying dataset vintages differ
entries.resolution_or_granularity: ADM0/ADM1/ADM2 location-level categories and source-layer references for eleven perils
entries.note: API exposes hazard scores by administrative division; official methodology describes classified levels as CC BY and distinct original-layer rights. Do not convert categories VLO/LOW/MED/HIG into physical intensities, probabilities of loss or calibrated insurance rates. Underlying model layers can overlap already-registered GFDRR sources. Software at https://github.com/GFDRR/thinkhazard is GPL-3.0 and is not the hazard-data licence.

entries.name: Maxar Open Data Program pre/post-disaster high-resolution imagery
entries.spatial_scope: global event activations, not continuous worldwide coverage
entries.temporal_scope: pre/post event releases by activation, with product-dependent acquisition dates
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Event-scoped cloud optimized imagery and STAC footprints, collection date and provider mosaic metadata
entries.note: The official AWS registry states CC BY-NC 4.0 and activation-only coverage. Distinguish image acquisition, processing, publication and controlled receipt. Commercial use, derived imagery and redistribution need separate rights review; no unapproved bytes in Git. Discovery from Microsoft's building-damage assessment workflow: https://github.com/microsoft/building-damage-assessment.

entries.name: xView2 xBD annotated pre/post disaster building damage dataset
entries.provider: xView2 / Maxar Open Data Program collaborators
entries.spatial_scope: selected disaster events across multiple countries, non-exhaustive
entries.temporal_scope: selected labelled disasters and static published benchmark splits
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Paired optical satellite images, building polygons and damage classes no/minor/major/destroyed
entries.note: Benchmark includes many building polygons across multiple perils; registration and noncommercial conditions apply to datasets, regardless of permissive code wrappers in TorchGeo or Microsoft. Prevent image-tile leakage across training/holdout and treat subjective damage labels as annotated observations, not insured economic losses. Discoverer: https://github.com/microsoft/building-damage-assessment.

entries.name: NASA JPL ARIA satellite radar damage proxy maps
entries.provider: NASA JPL / ARIA; contributing satellite partners
entries.spatial_scope: individual earthquake/disaster regions, includes 2023 Turkiye event
entries.temporal_scope: post-event acquisitions and derived maps with case-specific timestamps
entries.resolution_or_granularity: SAR coherence/change-based mapped areas; 2023 Turkiye release example has approximately 30 m pixels
entries.note: NASA JPL article links a 2023 earthquake damage-proxy-map download; ALOS-2 data involve JAXA and EO Singapore contributors. SAR change is not a confirmed collapsed building or financial loss; urban/vegetation bias, before/after dates and earthquake sequence timing must be captured. Evaluate each mapped original file licence separately.

entries.name: IFRC GO disaster event and field-report API v2
entries.provider: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
entries.spatial_scope: global national society reports, uneven coverage
entries.temporal_scope: reports and situation updates by event, publication and edit time
entries.resolution_or_granularity: IFRC event identity, appeals, situation/field reports, affected population and response indicators
entries.note: IFRC GO v2 situation_report docs provide created_at and event linkage. Some records are visibility-scoped; preserve permission and reporting qualifiers, not all textual attachments are reusable. Monty may derive its IFRC entries from the same API: do not count Monty and IFRC as independent evidence. Differentiate DREF from emergency appeals and field reports.

entries.name: UN OCHA CERF grants and humanitarian allocations API
entries.provider: UN OCHA Central Emergency Response Fund
entries.spatial_scope: global CERF supported operations, limited to funded countries/crises
entries.temporal_scope: historic and current allocations with funding/application release dates
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Applications, projects, country/agency/sector, allocation and donor-contribution values
entries.note: CERF amounts represent response grants and fundraising, NOT actual physical damage, insured losses or reconstruction cost. Match to original crisis event identifiers with versioned and uncertainty-aware mappings; guard double counting with ReliefWeb/IFRC. Confirm exact endpoint and redistribution policy before automated ingestion.

entries.name: UNDRR DesInventar Sendai country disaster loss inventories
entries.provider: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction / country custodians
entries.spatial_scope: country-dependent, historical inventories for participating countries
entries.temporal_scope: historic inventory vintages differ by jurisdiction; programme evolving toward DELTA
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Local-level disaster reports on fatalities, affected/damaged buildings and economic effects, with inconsistent definitions
entries.note: Country databases are contributed by national custodians; software Apache licensing DOES NOT license all underlying records. UNDRR describes a transition to DELTA Resilience. Confirm national version, original source, admin boundary and report-date uncertainty; economic damage is not insurer paid loss. Monty GCDB uses DesInventar as an upstream source.

entries.name: GLIDE global disaster identifier registry
entries.spatial_scope: global event identifiers where partner reporting exists
entries.temporal_scope: historical disaster identifiers since 2004, updated with reports
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Per-disaster hazard type, year, sequential number and ISO country components
entries.note: ADRC explicitly cautions that GLIDE IDs serve linking across disparate databases and discourages use of the registry for statistical secondary analysis. One GLIDE ID is not evidence of one physical seismic shock nor of one insurance occurrence; cross-border and multi-shock relations must remain explicit. Monty/MapAction/other upstream crosswalk evidence.

entries.name: International Charter Space and Major Disasters activation and map-product archive
entries.provider: International Charter: Space and Major Disasters
entries.spatial_scope: global supported disaster activations, selective event coverage
entries.temporal_scope: public activation archive since 2000, individual product acquisition and release dates vary
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Activation event links, disaster area, satellite-derived map products, mapped damage/flood/fire interpretation
entries.note: The public activation list and example maps do not authorize downloading/reusing underlying satellite acquisitions. Commercial rights and redistribution vary by original agency/provider and map product; modelled damage overlays do not constitute insured loss. Source used in MapAction disaster-impact harmonization.
